summary: This PR wires PROJEXA's Bearer-key v1 surface to real Permits/Drawings/Documents create+upload and a new Minutes-of-Meeting module, extracting a shared createDocumentRecord() upload path in document-service.ts and widening veri-meeting-service.ts's actor context from a hardcoded dbUser to the existing dbUser|apiKey ServiceActor union so API-key callers work. Verified directly rather than trusting the self-report: full `bunx tsc --noEmit` passes clean, `bunx eslint` on all eleven changed/added files is clean, the two new test files (meeting-minutes-pdf.test.ts, projexa-records-tenant-isolation.test.ts) pass (7/7), and the pre-existing voice-ticket-service.test.ts still passes after its type-only signature change. Every new/changed service call goes through withTenantContext with ctx.orgId, and the new tenant-isolation test exercises the real service functions (not a self-certifying mock) to prove org-scoped calls never cross-contaminate. Auth posture matches the codebase's established convention exactly: requireAuthOrApiKey for reads, requireRoleOrScope(ctx, "member", "write") for writes, and the ctx.dbUser?.id ?? ctx.apiKey?.id actor-id pattern is not new to this PR -- it's already used in ~30 other v1/projexa routes. Storage handling (signed URLs, bucket path sanitization via sanitizeFileName stripping slashes/traversal chars, 25MB size cap) mirrors the existing internal /api/documents upload path. No files under .github/workflows/** are touched, and the diff touches none of the tier2-triggering path patterns (migrations, schema.sql, auth/, permission/payment/billing/rls/security in path, or a heavy-deletion diff), so the deterministic tier1 classification is correct. Two minor, non-blocking issues are noted below for a follow-up.
issues: createDocumentRecord's externalUrl branch (document-service.ts) stores an arbitrary caller-supplied string as fileUrl with no protocol/format validation, and drawings/route.ts's toDrawingDto returns it directly as documentUrl for 3D-walkthrough entries when metadata.isExternalLink is set. If the PROJEXA frontend ever renders documentUrl as a clickable link without sanitizing the scheme, a member with write-scope could store a javascript:/data: URI as a stored-XSS vector for other org members who click it. The frontend that would render this link is outside this diff's scope, so exploitability can't be confirmed here, but a scheme allowlist (http/https only) on externalUrl at write time would close the gap cheaply.

The generic /v1/documents POST forwards caller-supplied `metadata` JSON straight into the stored record (document-service.ts's createDocumentRecord). A caller uploading a real file can also set metadata.isExternalLink: true themselves, causing the row to be misread later (e.g. by drawings/route.ts's toDrawingDto) as a link-only record and returning the raw internal storage object path as if it were a public URL. This isn't a data-exfiltration risk -- the storage bucket is private and the returned string isn't a fetchable URL -- but it produces a broken/inaccessible link in the UI. Consider stripping isExternalLink from caller-supplied metadata before merging, same as the code already does implicitly for the externalUrl branch.
